defs.def: upset because sth you hoped for has not happened or been as good, successful, etc. as you expected 失望的；沮丧的；失意的

ex.t: 他们对布拉德福德感到失望。

ex.s: You must have had some moments when you were disappointed.
ex.t: 你一定有过失望的时刻。

ex.s: This is something that even the highly successful Harry Potter movies can’t escape from, with fans of the books disappointed not to see some of their favourite characters in the movie versions.
ex.t: 这甚至是极为成功的《哈利\u00b7波特》电影也无法逃脱的，书迷们因为在电影中没有看到一些他们最喜欢的角色而感到失望。

ex.s: Disappointed by his behaviour, I said all this to my best friend.
ex.t: 我对他的行为感到失望，就把这一切告诉了我最好的朋友。

ex.s: And they feel very disappointed when they come to that final sentence.
ex.t: 当他们读到最后一句话时，感到非常失望。

ex.s: For the first few days, Kynan was always a bit disappointed that the cubs weren't there.
ex.t: 在最初的几天里，Kynan总是有点失望，因为幼崽不在那里。

ex.s: The city was crowded with disappointed people with no interest in settling down, and when they heard there were new gold discoveries in Alaska, they left Dawson City as quickly as they had come.
ex.t: 这座城市挤满了失望的人们，他们无意定居，当听说阿拉斯加有新的金矿发现时，他们以当初来的速度离开了道森城。
